notes: ROBOTS - THREE HOSTS WERE TOUCHED AND ALL THREE WERE CHECKED SEPARATELY (BATCH_BRIEF s1.3, robots is PER-HOST). (1) www.freedom.com.au - fetched FIRST, before any other request: HTTP 200, 1,367 bytes. Five groups: 'User-agent: *', and Disallow-all groups for CazoodleBot, MJ12bot, dotbot and Gigabot. NO Claude agent is named - a case-insensitive search for claude, anthropic, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web and anthropic-ai returns ZERO hits - so we fall under '*'. THE '*' GROUP CARRIES 'Crawl-delay: 5', WHICH I HONOURED: probe.MIN_GAP was raised from 2.0 to 5.0 s for every request to this host, for the whole company. The '*' disallows are /cart/, /checkout/, /online-payment-details/, /order-confirmation/, /search/, /my-account/, /els/, /medias/, */c/marketplace/, /items/, /*.pdf$ and a long list of query-string forms: ?gclid=, ?utm_source=, ?utm_campaign=, ?query=, ?sortCode=, ?yoReviews=, ?viewall=, ?sortid=, ?pp=, ?button=, ?filter=, ?reflist=, ?spJobID=, ?webSyncID=, ?item=, ?item_group=, ?size=, ?pid=, ?type=, ?in_recruiter=, ?region=, ?in_organid=, ?bvstate=, ?gclsrc=, ?istCompanyId, ?null and ?q=. I requested NONE of them: no /search/, no /medias/, no marketplace path (note the site DOES carry marketplace-* category tags internally - I never fetched a */c/marketplace/ URL), no /items/, and NOT ONE query string of any kind on this host. Every www URL I fetched is a bare path. Note also that '?viewall=' and '?filter=' being disallowed rules out the obvious facet/view-all route to a count - which is part of why the count had to come from the storefront's own product API. (2) api-prod.freedom.com.au - Freedom's own OCC/commerce backend, the host the storefront's own <meta name='occ-backend-base-url'> points at. Its robots.txt returns HTTP 404, i.e. NO robots file exists and nothing is disallowed. Checked before the first request to it. (3) freedomfurnitureproduction1s4nmz28u.org.coveo.com - the Coveo Commerce host the PLP actually renders from. robots.txt HTTP 200. It names NO Claude agent, and its 'User-agent: *' group is an explicit ALLOW-LIST followed by 'Disallow: /': Allow /rest/search, /rest/organizations/*/commerce/v2/listing, /commerce/v2/search, /querySuggest, /productSuggest, /facet, /recommendations. THE ONLY ENDPOINT I USED IS /rest/organizations/*/commerce/v2/listing, WHICH IS EXPLICITLY ALLOWED BY NAME. I requested nothing else on that host. This is the opposite of the SR 145 / QVC situation: it is not a Disallow-all host being reached indirectly, it is a host that explicitly permits exactly the endpoint used. ACCESS: no bot wall, no interstitial, no 403, no 429, no campaign parameters, no r.jina.ai, no browser automation, no third-party proxy. WHY AN API WAS NEEDED AT ALL, AND THE LADDER THAT GOT THERE - documented because it took real work. freedom.com.au is an SAP Spartacus ANGULAR SPA. Its category pages return HTTP 200 with a full <ng-state> transfer-state block, but that block's /cx-state/product slice is EMPTY ({'search':{'results':{}},...}): the product grid, the product count and the pagination are ALL client-rendered. I verified this rather than assuming - I parsed the entire 713 KB ng-state to leaves (14,430 values) and searched every key name for count/total/number/qty: the only matches are defaultNumberOfFilters, shownProductCount, subMenuColumnCount and totalDisplay, none of which is a product total. There is NO rendered '<n> Products' string, no JSON-LD ItemList, no numberOfItems. So per WORKER_BRIEF step 4 the count had to come from 'the storefront's own product API (the one the PLP itself renders from)'. Route 1 - the OCC backend. From the page's occ-backend-base-url meta and the endpoint prefix '/greenlitrest/v2/' found in main-D2JCL3R5.js, the OCC search endpoint is https://api-prod.freedom.com.au/greenlitrest/v2/freedomfurniture/products/search. It is REACHABLE and the host is open (a control call to .../products/13328545?fields=DEFAULT returns HTTP 200 with a full product), but EVERY form of the search call returns HTTP 400 {'message':'IndexedType cannot be null'} - I tried the stock Spartacus ':relevance:allCategories:<code>' query, ':relevance:category:<code>', a bare code, a free-text term, '*', with and without lang/curr, with and without the app's own 745-character fields string, with device/viewAll/sort/currentPage/selectedDeliveryArea, and with an x-user-id header. The solr index behind that endpoint is not resolvable from outside; the site has moved PLP search to Coveo. Documented as a dead end, not silently dropped. Route 2 - the Coveo Commerce API, which IS what the PLP renders from. Freedom's own backend issues the public search token at https://api-prod.freedom.com.au/greenlitrest/v2/freedomfurniture/coveo/token (HTTP 200), which identifies organization 'freedomfurnitureproduction1s4nmz28u'; the trackingId 'freedom_au' comes from the site's own baseSite config in ng-state (coveoTrackingId). POST to the allow-listed /rest/organizations/{org}/commerce/v2/listing with {'trackingId':'freedom_au','language':'en','country':'AU','currency':'AUD','context':{'view':{'url':...}}} returns the exact listing the PLP shows, including pagination.totalProducts. THE LISTING KEY - and the canonical proof that it is the same node. A listing config exists for the SHORT category URL https://www.freedom.com.au/c/<code> and NOT for the long nav path (the long path returns LISTING_CONFIGURATION_DOES_NOT_EXIST). I did not assume the two are the same category: I fetched https://www.freedom.com.au/c/bath-accessories directly and it returns HTTP 200 with H1 'Bath Accessories' and <link rel=canonical> = https://www.freedom.com.au/bed-and-bath/bathroom/c/bath-accessories - the site itself declares the short form an alias of the long form. The short form is therefore a FETCH DETAIL ONLY; the URL written into rows[] is the clean canonical nav path, exactly as the campaign-parameter rule requires for an equivalent situation. TREE SOURCE - FREEDOM'S OWN NAVIGATION, cross-checked against its own category sitemap. The home-page mega-menu server-renders the full category tree as hrefs; https://www.freedom.com.au/sitemap.xml -> categorysitemap.xml gives 234 category URLs. The two disagree in BOTH directions and I used the union: the sitemap does NOT contain the deeper mirror nodes (bathroom-mirrors, round-mirror, arched-mirror, wall-mirror, full-length-mirror, mirrors) that the mega-menu exposes, while the mega-menu is the only place the Bathroom Mirrors node appears at all. The Bathroom branch is BED & BATH > Bathroom > {Bath Accessories, Bath Mats, Bath Towels} - three children in the mega-menu, the same three in categorysitemap.xml, and independently the same three confirmed by product-tag enumeration of the parent (below). Bathroom Mirrors sits on a different branch, WALL ART, MIRRORS & LIGHTING > Wall Decor & Mirrors > Mirrors > Bathroom Mirrors. QTY: pagination.totalProducts from the storefront's OWN Coveo Commerce listing - the identical call the PLP makes. No estimate, no aggregation, no parent's number reused for a child, no pagination multiplication. VERIFICATION - ENUMERATION TO EXHAUSTION, which is the strongest form WORKER_BRIEF step 4 allows. I paged each node to the end and counted DISTINCT permanentids: Bath Accessories 81 stated / 81 enumerated; Bath Mats 28 / 28; Bath Towels 115 / 115; Bathroom 249 / 249. FOUR nodes of visibly different size (28, 81, 115, 249), 4/4 exact, zero drift - so the payload total is the true product count and not a cap or an estimate. A single page-size-100 call to Bath Accessories also returns exactly 81 products in one response, an independent confirmation of the same figure by a different page size. SECOND, INDEPENDENT CHECK - PARENT = EXACT SUM OF CHILDREN, proved by product identity rather than arithmetic: of the parent Bathroom node's 249 enumerated products, exactly 81 carry the ec_category tag 'bath-accessories', 28 carry 'bath-mats', 115 carry 'bath-towels' and 25 carry 'laundry-hampers', with ZERO overlap between the four sets and ZERO products outside them. 81+28+115+25 = 249. That both confirms the four totals and identifies the 25-product remainder as the cross-tagged Laundry Hampers node, which is routed out. DISCRIMINATION: the totals returned across the 17 nodes queried are 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 25, 28, 29, 76, 81, 83, 90, 115, 249, 321, 402, 1421, 3385 - no site-wide constant, no round-number cap (no 100/500/1000 anywhere), and the endpoint distinguishes a real empty node (0) from a non-existent one (HTTP 404 LISTING_CONFIGURATION_DOES_NOT_EXIST), which is what let me classify Bathroom Mirrors correctly. H1 and rel=canonical were read on every recorded and reviewed node; the one recorded leaf is self-canonical at the URL written into rows[]. Freedom does not expose those as separate listing URLs - there is no bathrobe node in the nav or the sitemap - so the node is recorded whole, on its dominant primary product type, with this caveat stated rather than hidden. Its recorded 81 is the storefront's own figure for its own node. DEDUP - OPTION 1, run on every candidate URL and every rel=canonical target. The exclusion index holds 105 freedom.com.au keys. ZERO hits on the recorded leaf and zero on any node inside the Bathroom branch (bathroom, bath-accessories, bath-mats, bath-towels, bathroom-mirrors, laundry-hampers are all absent from the index). SEVEN HITS, all in review[] and never in rows[]: the ENTIRE decor-mirror branch - Mirrors 402, Wall Mirrors 321, Arched Mirrors 90, Full Length Mirrors 83, Round Mirrors 76 and Kids Mirrors 5, all Final.xlsx (Home Decor pass) - plus Vanity Tables 29 (Furniture.xlsx). CANONICAL-ALIAS BLIND SPOT (BATCH_BRIEF s4a) CHECKED: Round Mirrors and Arched Mirrors canonicalise to DIFFERENT URLs from the ones the nav links (.../wall-decor-and-mirrors/mirrors/c/round-mirrors, plural, under a /mirrors/ segment) - but the index holds the nav form, so both forms were tested and both resolve to already-extracted records. Locale/cross-host blind spots (b) and (c) do not arise: freedom.com.au is a single-locale AU storefront, the index holds no freedom.co.nz or other variant host, and although the baseSite config also defines a New Zealand site (coveoTrackingId freedom_nz), it is not this company and was not walked. WHAT IS ABSENT FROM THIS RETAILER, evidenced rather than assumed. Freedom is a furniture and homewares retailer, not a bathroom-fittings retailer. It sells NO baths or bathtubs, NO toilets/WCs, NO bidets, NO basins or wash-basins, NO bathroom taps or faucets, NO showers, shower heads, shower mixers, shower enclosures or screens, NO bathroom vanity units, wash-stands or bathroom cabinets, and - right now - NO bathroom mirrors (the node exists and is empty). Evidence: the full mega-menu walk, the complete 234-URL categorysitemap.xml, and direct probes of the Coveo listing configuration for the codes bath-linen, towels, bathroom-storage, bathroom-accessories, toilet-roll-holders, shower, shower-curtains, bath-robes and bathroom-storage-au - EVERY one returns LISTING_CONFIGURATION_DOES_NOT_EXIST, i.e. no such category exists on this storefront. RESULT: 1 grouping row + 1 leaf row; 16 review entries (7 dedup hits, 1 empty node, 3 textile routings, 1 storage routing, 1 hidden tag with no URL, 1 sale page, 2 parent/department exclusions). A single-leaf result is the correct answer here, not a shortfall: everything else Freedom files under Bathroom is towels and bath mats (Textile) or laundry hampers (Storage), and its entire mirror branch was already taken by the Home Decor pass.
